rewrites.//: Token exchange, same-origin. The frontend calls /oauth/:provider/:action; this maps it onto the serverless function. MUST come before the SPA fallback below — rewrites are matched in order, and the fallback would otherwise swallow it and return index.html.

SPA fallback. This is what makes /connect/callback resolve — without it Vercel 404s on a path with no file, and the OAuth redirect dies before the app ever loads. api/ and oauth/ are excluded so the function routes above still win.

headers.//: The page must not be framable: an attacker framing the connect screen could trick someone into authorising a provider (clickjacking).

connect-src is 'self' plus the provider APIs the browser calls directly. Token exchange is same-origin now, so no third-party backend origin appears here at all — that is the security dividend of dropping the cross-origin backend.
headers.value: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://open.spotify.com https://www.youtube.com https://s.ytimg.com; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: https:; media-src 'none'; connect-src 'self' https://api.spotify.com https://www.googleapis.com; frame-src https://open.spotify.com https://www.youtube.com https://www.youtube-nocookie.com; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'

headers.//: Token responses carry credentials. Nothing may cache them — not the browser, not Vercel's edge, not an intermediary.
